The feeder identifier uniquely identifies a specific electrical grid segment serving a defined geographic area. In small or rural areas, a single feeder may serve only a handful of consumers, making it a quasi-identifier that could be used to narrow down to specific households or businesses. Under data protection principles, this constitutes an indirect identifier that, when combined with other data, could re-identify individuals. Generalization or pseudonymization is recommended.

The substation identifier identifies a specific electrical substation serving a geographic region. While broader than a feeder, in smaller networks it can still narrow down to a specific community or neighborhood. Combined with feeder data, it creates a hierarchical location identifier that increases re-identification risk. Pseudonymization is advisable to prevent linkage attacks.

The date column provides temporal context for the measurements. While it is historical data, by itself it does not identify any individual. It is a common temporal attribute present in all records and does not constitute personal data. However, when combined with very granular consumption data for a small area, it could contribute to pattern-based re-identification, but the standalone risk is low.

This is an aggregate count of housing units served by the feeder. It does not identify any specific household or individual. It is a statistical summary of infrastructure capacity. The value (e.g., 70) is too coarse to identify any particular resident. No direct personal data is contained.

This is an aggregate count of industrial and commercial units connected to the feeder. It is a statistical infrastructure metric that does not identify any specific business or individual. The count (e.g., 11) is too general to constitute personal data or enable re-identification of specific entities.

This represents the total installed capacity of storage heaters across all consumers on the feeder. It is an aggregate infrastructure measurement (144.4 kW) that does not identify any individual consumer or household. It is a network-level capacity parameter, not personal data.

This is the aggregate installed capacity of heat pumps on the feeder (2.1 kW). It is a network-level infrastructure parameter that does not identify any specific consumer. The value is too small and aggregate to constitute personal data or enable re-identification.

This represents the total installed capacity of electric heaters across the feeder (28.8 kW). It is an aggregate infrastructure measurement that does not identify any individual. It is a network planning parameter, not personal data.

This is the aggregate installed capacity of hot water tanks on the feeder (6.0 kW). It is a network-level infrastructure parameter that does not identify any specific consumer or household. No personal data is contained in this aggregate measurement.

This represents the total installed capacity of flow-type heaters on the feeder (42.0 kW). It is an aggregate infrastructure measurement that does not identify any individual consumer. It is a network capacity parameter used for grid planning.

This is the aggregate installed capacity of EV chargers on the feeder (0.0 kW in this case). It is a network-level infrastructure parameter. Even if non-zero, it would represent total capacity across all consumers and would not identify any specific vehicle owner or individual.

This represents the total capacity of public lighting on the feeder (10.0 kW). Public lighting is municipal infrastructure and does not relate to any individual consumer. It is a purely public infrastructure parameter with no personal data implications.

This is the aggregate installed capacity of other/miscellaneous consumers on the feeder (254.5 kW). It is a network-level infrastructure measurement that does not identify any specific consumer. It is a residual category in grid planning and contains no personal data.

This represents the total installed capacity of battery storage systems on the feeder (0.0 kW). It is an aggregate infrastructure parameter that does not identify any specific consumer or installation. No personal data is contained.

This is the aggregate installed capacity of photovoltaic systems on the feeder (0.0 kW). It is a network-level infrastructure measurement. Even if non-zero, it represents total PV capacity across all consumers and does not identify any specific household or business.

This represents the total installed capacity of combined heat and power (CHP) systems on the feeder (10.8 kW). It is an aggregate infrastructure parameter that does not identify any specific consumer or installation. No personal data is contained.

The feeder identifier is an operational asset code used for grid management. It does not directly identify an individual and is presented in aggregated form across many households, so it is not personal data.
The substation code is a technical asset identifier, not linked to any natural person. It is used for infrastructure monitoring only.
The date of measurement is a temporal attribute of the dataset. It does not identify a person and is required for time‑series analysis.
